message: thread_local! turmoil_net::CURRENT is written from 10 functions of its own module: turmoil_net::EnterGuard::deliver, turmoil_net::EnterGuard::drop, turmoil_net::EnterGuard::egress_all, turmoil_net::EnterGuard::evaluate, turmoil_net::EnterGuard::set_current, turmoil_net::Net::enter, turmoil_net::install_rule, turmoil_net::set_current, turmoil_net::sys, turmoil_net::uninstall_rule
why: RefCell::borrow_mut counted as a write to the static: only Net::enter and EnterGuard::drop rebind the slot, the other 8 borrow to reach into the Net, and a thread_local guarded by an RAII EnterGuard is the sanctioned scoped-context pattern.

message: turmoil_fs::DirData::new (one line) is called once, from turmoil_fs::FsState::new: fold it into the caller
why: Canonical Rust `new` delegating to a `with_mode` variant; folding it spells the documented 0o755 default at an unrelated caller and leaves the type without a `new`.

message: turmoil_fs::shim::std::fs::canonicalize returns Error but its `# Errors` section never names it
why: The Errors section names only nonexistent paths and non-directory components, but the body also returns ELOOP (too many levels of symbolic links) and symbolic link loop detected, and never returns the non-directory error it claims.

message: turmoil_fs::shim::std::fs::remove_dir_all returns Error but its `# Errors` section never names it
why: The Errors section lists all three conditions the body returns (missing path, not a directory, an entry that cannot be removed); the rule wants the literal type name `Error` spelled, which is not what an `# Errors` section is for.
